title: Chapter 110: The Same Dream
html:
“The same condition as that boy? Does he also enjoy Haunted Houses?” Doctor Gao had caught Chen Ge’s interest.

“Low spirits, occasional outbursts, and a preference for dark, isolated places because they make him feel safe. I can’t say whether he likes Haunted Houses.” Doctor Gao stepped aside, revealing the young man behind him. “This is my student, Men Nan. He first came to me about his condition three weeks ago.”

The slender man in his twenties had high cheekbones, dark circles beneath his eyes, and a face locked with tension. Sweat beaded on his forehead despite the mild sunlight. He kept his head bowed, unable to meet anyone’s gaze.

“Surname Men?” Chen Ge tried to make conversation. “That’s rare, nice to meet you.”

The reaction was peculiar. Without lifting his head, Men Nan flicked his eyes over Chen Ge and murmured, “Nice to meet you.”

After studying him, Chen Ge drew Doctor Gao aside. “Why bring him here? If you expect him to enter the Haunted House, I can’t take responsibility for what happens.”

“Men Nan was a cheerful, confident child, one of my brightest students. He is incredibly talented in the field of personality psychology.”

“Personality psychology?”

“It is a branch of psychology concerned with understanding patterns of human behavior.”

“Okay.” Chen Ge nodded even though he still did not quite get it.

“His symptoms appeared without warning three weeks ago. Psychological disorders usually have a trigger, often connected to family or environment. Men Nan lives alone, and nothing in his circumstances has changed, so I’m at a loss,” Doctor Gao whispered, careful not to be overheard.

“Repeated sessions have brought no improvement. In fact, he is deteriorating. He has always been patient, but lately his moods turn violent without warning. He fought a classmate because the animal patterns on a curtain did not match, and attacked a stranger because he kept getting a different number each time he counted the sesame seeds on the man’s bun.”

“Those are unusual reasons to become violent.”

“Under enough psychological strain, the smallest irritation can trigger an emotional explosion. His behavior showed me how deeply he was suffering.”

“But why would you bring him to me?” Chen Ge looked at Doctor Gao and Men Nan. The special visitor was probably one of them.

“Wang Xin has improved dramatically. Symptoms that had worsened for years eased after one meeting with you,” Doctor Gao said. “I’m not too proud to accept an unconventional method if it helps the patient. Men Nan’s suffering troubles me deeply, and I would like your assistance.”

“Go on.” Chen Ge did not refuse outright.

“Can you do for Men Nan what you did for Wang Xin? From what we know, he, Wang Xin, and the boy we discussed all suffer from similar conditions.”

Chen Ge hesitated. He had not expected this request. His success with Wang Xin must have impressed the senior psychologist more than he realized.

But Chen Ge knew the truth. He had helped Wang Xin only because the Pen Spirit revealed their history and personally intervened. The method belonged to that case and could not simply be repeated.

“Would that be a problem?” Doctor Gao noticed his hesitation. “If I’m asking too much, forget it. I’m only searching for another possibility. This young man has immense talent, but long-term medication could affect both body and mind. I fear it would damage his future.”

“It may be difficult, but not impossible. If you want my help, tell me more about him.” Chen Ge still did not refuse. One of the two was the special visitor, and every special visitor was a hidden opportunity he could not ignore.

“Then I’ll thank you in advance on his behalf.” Doctor Gao smiled and called Men Nan over. “Tell us what has been troubling you.”

Men Nan kept his head lowered regardless of whom he addressed, as though an invisible hand pressed against his skull.

When the young man remained silent, Doctor Gao sighed and continued for him. “Three weeks ago, he came to me because he suspected depression. We are both trained professionals, and after evaluating him for an afternoon, I found that his symptoms did not match ordinary depression. He seemed agitated and exhausted, nothing more. Then his condition worsened. He could pass an entire day without speaking and become violent at the slightest irritation. After considerable analysis, I reached a conclusion he refused to admit: he is terrified of something buried in his own mind.

“I suspect a fear disorder, but nothing in his environment explains it. After repeated questioning, he finally admitted the truth.” Doctor Gao regarded his student with concern. “For the past three weeks, he has had the same dream every night.”

The mention of the dream made Men Nan shudder. More than anything, he feared confronting it.

“What kind of dream?” Chen Ge had imagined many scary scenarios, but Doctor Gao’s answer surprised him.

“He dreamed about washing his hair.”

“Washing his hair?” Chen Ge did not know what to say.

“I’ll let him explain the rest.” Doctor Gao placed a reassuring hand on Men Nan’s shoulder.

After a long silence, Men Nan spoke. “It’s always the same dream, but every night it becomes clearer. Soon I’ll be able to see the person’s face.”

His voice was raw, as though his throat had been burned.

“Who is this person? There’s another person in your dream?”

“Yes. He always stands beside me and watches me wash my hair. He feels dangerous. I know the moment I close my eyes, he’ll rush forward and strangle me.”
